## Purpose and audience

This draft is for provincial and regional public-health decision makers. It describes where published apparent opioid toxicity death rates and the reported male-to-female rate gap warrant closer review. It does not identify causes or recommend a specific policy or funding decision.

## Question

How did reported crude opioid toxicity death rates vary across Canadian
jurisdictions from 2016 to 2025, and how did the male-to-female rate ratio
vary? This project update presents the current descriptive evidence for provincial and regional public-health readers.

## Data source and provenance

The analysis uses the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC)'s public *Opioid- and Stimulant-related Harms in Canada* surveillance release. The group committed the September 22, 2026 CSV snapshot for a repeatable analysis and accessed it on October 26, 2026. Definitions, reporting changes and coverage follow [PHAC technical notes](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/substance-related-harms/opioids-stimulants/technical-notes.html). The source contains aggregate surveillance values; one analytic row below represents a region and year.

## Setup

The source is the fixed public aggregate PHAC file at
`data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv`, identified in the group's intake card as
the September 22, 2026 release, accessed October 26, 2026.

One analytic row represents a region-year, not a person or death.
We select Opioids, Deaths, By year, 2016-2025, and Crude rate, retaining
overall rates and the reported male and female sex categories.
Quarterly data, partial 2026 data, other harms, and stimulants are excluded.
Canada is a separate reference series, not an additional province.

```{r}
#| label: prepare-region-year-data
# AI prompt: Read the PHAC CSV as text using repository-relative paths.
# Select annual opioid-death crude rates for 2016-2025 and reshape overall,
# male, and female values into unique region-years. Preserve zeroes and
# suppression labels, calculate ratios only with a positive female denominator,
# and flag partial-year coverage and the specified 2025 reporting changes.
# Verified: Checked source filters, unique keys, numeric values, zeroes, and raw suppression labels.
# M3 revision prompt summary: output-path change only.
# AI prompt: Keep the M2 data preparation unchanged, but write its generated
# CSV outputs under milestones/m3-project-update/submission/outputs.
# Verified: Compared this chunk with M2; only out_dir changed. Confirmed the
# fixed CSV hash and generated M3 CSV outputs after rendering.

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)

roots <- c(".", "../../..")
repo_root <- roots[file.exists(file.path(roots, "data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv"))][1]

if (is.na(repo_root)) stop("Cannot find data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv.")

out_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "milestones/m3-project-update/submission/outputs")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

source_df <- read_csv(
  file.path(repo_root, "data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character()
)

selected <- source_df |>
  filter(
    Substance == "Opioids",
    Source == "Deaths",
    Time_Period == "By year",
    Year_Quarter %in% as.character(2016:2025),
    Unit == "Crude rate",
    (Specific_Measure == "Overall numbers" & Disaggregator == "") |
      (Specific_Measure == "Sex" & Disaggregator %in% c("Male", "Female"))
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Region,
    Year = as.integer(Year_Quarter),
    measure = case_when(
      Specific_Measure == "Overall numbers" ~ "overall",
      Disaggregator == "Male" ~ "male",
      TRUE ~ "female"
    ),
    raw = trimws(Value)
  )

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(selected[c("Region", "Year", "measure")]))

is_numeric <- grepl("^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$", selected$raw)

selected$rate <- NA_real_
selected$rate[is_numeric] <- as.numeric(selected$raw[is_numeric])

selected$status <- case_when(
  is_numeric ~ "Reported",
  selected$raw == "Suppr." ~ "Suppressed",
  selected$raw == "n/a" ~ "Unavailable",
  TRUE ~ "Unexpected"
)

stopifnot(!any(selected$status == "Unexpected"))

panel <- selected |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = measure,
    values_from = c(raw, rate, status),
    names_glue = "{measure}_{.value}"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    partial_year = Region == "Nunavut" & Year == 2023,
    definition_change =
      Region %in% c("British Columbia", "Quebec", "Canada") & Year == 2025,
    ratio_rate = if_else(
      !is.na(male_rate) & !is.na(female_rate) & female_rate > 0,
      male_rate / female_rate,
      NA_real_
    ),
    ratio_status = case_when(
      male_status == "Suppressed" |
        female_status == "Suppressed" ~ "Suppressed",
      male_status == "Unavailable" |
        female_status == "Unavailable" ~ "Unavailable",
      female_rate == 0 ~ "Zero denominator",
      !is.na(ratio_rate) ~ "Reported",
      TRUE ~ "Unexpected"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Region, Year)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(panel[c("Region", "Year")]))
stopifnot(nrow(panel) == 140, n_distinct(panel$Region) == 14)

kable(
  data.frame(
    Step = c(
      "Source CSV rows",
      "Selected rate records",
      "Unique region-years"
    ),
    N = c(nrow(source_df), nrow(selected), nrow(panel))
  ),
  caption = "Selection flow: three rate records become one region-year."
)
```

## Methods: selection and exclusions

The inclusion rules and the exceptions below were set before interpreting the figures.

## Cohort

Table 1 uses the common calendar window 2016–2024 for every region. The
2025 values remain in the availability audit, endpoint table, and annual
figures, but not in Table 1: British Columbia, Quebec, and Canada have
2025 reporting changes, so including that year for only some regions
would weaken comparisons. Nunavut 2023 is also excluded from Table 1
because reporting covers only part of that year. A common window does
not create complete data: the table shows the number of reported years
separately for each region and measure.

```{r}
#| label: summary-eligibility
# M3 revision prompt summary, based on the M2 feedback.
# AI prompt: Revise the M2 summary-eligibility chunk to use the same
# 2016-2024 calendar window for every region after checking data availability.
# Exclude partial-year Nunavut 2023, retain all 2016-2025 rows in the
# availability audit and figures, and display the Table 1 selection counts.
# Verified: Checked 126 region-years in 2016-2024 before the Nunavut
# exclusion, 125 afterward, and the 2025 and Nunavut cautions against
# the source data and PHAC technical notes.

summary_df <- panel |>
  filter(Year <= 2024, !partial_year)

kable(
  data.frame(
    Step = c(
      "Selected region-years",
      "2025 rows outside common window",
      "Partial-year Nunavut 2023 exclusion",
      "Table 1 region-years"
    ),
    N = c(
      nrow(panel),
      sum(panel$Year == 2025),
      sum(panel$partial_year),
      nrow(summary_df)
    )
  ),
  caption = "The 2016–2025 panel remains available for the audit and annual figures."
)
```

## Missingness

Suppression and unavailability are kept distinct. Reported zeroes stay zero;
they are not missing. A ratio requires two reported rates and a positive
female rate. Ratios use rounded published rates and are approximate.

The denominator below is all 140 selected region-years, including 2025
and records excluded from Table 1. Missingness is not assumed random.

```{r}
#| label: missingness-and-export
# AI prompt: Before exclusions, summarize availability of overall, male, female,
# and ratio values across all selected region-years. Include numeric and missing
# counts, missing percentages, and separate counts for suppression, unavailable
# values, and zero denominators. Display and export missingness-summary.csv.
# Verified: Compared all availability categories and percentages with separate base-R counts and the exported CSV.

measures <- c("overall", "male", "female", "ratio")

missingness <- bind_rows(lapply(measures, function(m) {
  v <- panel[[paste0(m, "_rate")]]
  s <- panel[[paste0(m, "_status")]]

  data.frame(
    Measure = m,
    Region_year_N = nrow(panel),
    Numeric_N = sum(!is.na(v)),
    Missing_N = sum(is.na(v)),
    Missing_percent = round(100 * mean(is.na(v)), 1),
    Suppressed_N = sum(s == "Suppressed"),
    Unavailable_N = sum(s == "Unavailable"),
    Zero_denominator_N = sum(s == "Zero denominator")
  )
}))

write_csv(missingness, file.path(out_dir, "missingness-summary.csv"))

kable(
  missingness,
  caption = "Availability before summary exclusions; N counts region-years."
)
```

## Table 1: compact regional summary

We checked the available annual overall, female, male, and ratio values
for every region before selecting 2016–2024 as the common Table 1
window. Most regions have nine reported years for all four measures.
Within this window, Yukon has four reported female, male, and ratio
years; the Northwest Territories has five. Their published overall
series have nine years, but the Table 1 overall means are restricted to
the same four and five years, respectively, so within-region means
cover matched years. Prince Edward Island has no reported sex-specific
rates or defined ratios. Nunavut has three reported full-year values
for the first three measures, all in 2016–2018, and no defined ratios.
These differences appear as `n` in each cell. An overall rate is
published independently and cannot reveal suppressed sex-specific rates.

Each cell gives mean (sample SD) across included annual values and the
number of contributing years. Rates are crude deaths per 100,000;
the ratio is unitless and calculated from rounded published rates.
These arithmetic means are not pooled-period mortality rates.
Canada is PHAC's separate national series, never an average of
provincial rates. Suppressed and unavailable values are not imputed;
reported zeroes are retained.

```{r}
#| label: table1-and-export
# M3 revision prompt summary, based on the M2 feedback.
# AI prompt: Revise the M2 Table 1 chunk into one row per region and four
# columns: overall, female, male, and male-to-female ratio. Use the common
# 2016-2024 window, show mean (sample SD) and contributing-year n in each
# cell, remove year lists, and explain remaining n differences in the
# caption. Retain matched-year overall means for Yukon and the Northwest
# Territories and PEI's independently reported overall series.
# Verified: Audited availability across all 14 regions and four measures;
# independently recalculated all 56 exported table cells from the CSV and
# checked the matched-year counts (Yukon n=4; Northwest Territories n=5).

mean_sd <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]

  if (!length(x)) return("Not available")

  if (length(x) == 1) {
    return(sprintf("%.2f (SD unavailable)", x))
  }

  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(x), sd(x))
}

table1_long <- summary_df |>
  mutate(both_sex_rates_reported = !is.na(male_rate) & !is.na(female_rate)) |>
  select(Region, Year, both_sex_rates_reported, all_of(paste0(measures, "_rate"))) |>
  pivot_longer(
    ends_with("_rate"),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Rate"
  ) |>
  mutate(Measure = sub("_rate$", "", Measure)) |>
  filter(
    !(Measure == "overall" & Region %in% c("Yukon", "Northwest Territories")) |
      both_sex_rates_reported
  ) |>
  group_by(Region, Measure) |>
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(Rate)),
    Mean_SD = mean_sd(Rate),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Cell = if_else(n == 0, "Not available (n=0)",
                   paste0(Mean_SD, "; n=", n)),
    Measure = recode(
      Measure,
      overall = "Overall",
      female = "Female",
      male = "Male",
      ratio = "Male-to-female ratio"
    )
  )

table1 <- table1_long |>
  select(Region, Measure, Cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Measure, values_from = Cell) |>
  select(Region, Overall, Female, Male, `Male-to-female ratio`)

write_csv(table1, file.path(out_dir, "table1.csv"))

kable(
  table1,
  caption = "Table 1. Mean (sample SD); n = contributing years within 2016–2024. Nunavut 2023 is excluded as a partial year. Yukon and Northwest Territories overall means use only years with both sex-specific rates reported (n = 4 and 5) for within-region alignment. Other n differences reflect suppression or unavailability. Rates are crude deaths per 100,000; the ratio is unitless."
)
```

## Results: annual comparisons

### Endpoint comparison

This table compares published overall crude rates in 2016, 2024, and 2025.
Source labels remain visible instead of being replaced by zero. The 2025
rates for British Columbia, Quebec, and Canada are flagged because of
reporting changes; these endpoints do not describe the full trajectory.

```{r}
#| label: endpoint-comparison
# AI prompt: Compare each region's published overall crude rates in 2016,
# 2024, and 2025. Preserve source suppression and unavailable labels and flag
# reporting changes without implying endpoints describe the full trajectory.
# Verified: Compared displayed values with the source CSV and PHAC notes.

endpoints <- panel |>
  filter(Year %in% c(2016, 2024, 2025)) |>
  select(Region, Year, overall_raw) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year,
    values_from = overall_raw,
    names_prefix = "Rate_"
  )

kable(
  endpoints,
  caption = "Published overall crude rates per 100,000; 2025 reporting changes are flagged in the text."
)
```

In PHAC's Canada series, the reported overall rate is 7.8 in 2016 and 16.2
in 2024; its 2025 value has a reporting-change caution. This is a clear endpoint difference in the published national crude rates, not proof of a monotonic rise or a population-adjusted effect. These comparisons do
not imply a steady increase in every intervening year. The annual figures
show the intervening values. For the secondary question, Table 1 summarizes
defined annual male-to-female ratios; unavailable ratios do not imply equal
rates.

### Figure 1: annual reported crude death rates

Each panel shows a province or territory in blue and PHAC's Canada rate in
grey. Nunavut 2023 is omitted from the full-year plot. Triangles identify
the 2025 reporting cautions for BC, Quebec, and Canada; their 2025 points
are disconnected from earlier lines. Other 2025 observations remain in the
plot. The panels use the same zero-based vertical scale.

```{r}
#| label: figure-overall-rates
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-cap: "Annual published crude death rates per 100,000. Blue: jurisdiction; grey: PHAC Canada reference. Gaps preserve suppressed, unavailable, or partial-year data. Triangles mark 2025 reporting cautions; recent data may be revised."
# AI prompt: Follow our M1 plan with one panel per province or territory,
# blue annual crude-rate trends, and a grey PHAC Canada reference. Preserve gaps,
# omit partial-year Nunavut 2023, and show flagged 2025 values as disconnected
# triangles. Use common zero-based axes and explain colours and markers.
# Verified: Checked plotted values against source rates and confirmed partial-year omissions and disconnected caution points.

plot_panel <- panel |>
  mutate(
    plot_rate = if_else(partial_year, NA_real_, overall_rate),
    line_rate = if_else(definition_change, NA_real_, plot_rate),
    plot_ratio = if_else(partial_year, NA_real_, ratio_rate),
    line_ratio = if_else(definition_change, NA_real_, plot_ratio)
  )

jurisdictions <- plot_panel |>
  filter(Region != "Canada")

canada_reference <- plot_panel |>
  filter(Region == "Canada") |>
  select(-Region)

ggplot(jurisdictions, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_line(
    data = canada_reference,
    aes(y = line_rate),
    colour = "grey65",
    linewidth = 0.5,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = canada_reference,
    aes(y = plot_rate, shape = definition_change),
    colour = "grey65",
    size = 1,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = line_rate),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = plot_rate, shape = definition_change),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 1.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Region, ncol = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 17),
    labels = c("Other years", "2025 reporting caution")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2016, 2019, 2022, 2025)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.07))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Reported crude deaths per 100,000",
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```

### Figure 2: male-to-female rate ratios

A ratio above 1 means the reported male rate is higher than the female
rate. Ratios are undefined when either rate is suppressed or unavailable,
or the female rate is zero. Prince Edward Island and Nunavut have no
defined ratios in this release. Flagged 2025 points are separated here
as a conservative reporting caution, too.

```{r}
#| label: figure-sex-ratios
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-cap: "Male-to-female crude-rate ratios calculated from rounded published rates. The dashed line marks equal reported rates. Gaps and absent ratios do not imply equality. Reported sex categories are not gender identity."
# AI prompt: Plot annual male-to-female rate ratios by province or territory
# using common zero-based axes and a dashed reference at 1. Preserve gaps and
# disconnected flagged 2025 points, label panels with no defined ratios, and
# explain that missing ratios do not imply equality or describe gender identity.
# Verified: Checked ratios against male and female rates, positive denominators, missing-data gaps, and empty-panel labels.

no_ratio <- jurisdictions |>
  group_by(Region) |>
  summarise(
    no_values = all(is.na(plot_ratio)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(no_values)

ggplot(jurisdictions, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey55"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = line_ratio),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    linewidth = 0.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = plot_ratio, shape = definition_change),
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 1.6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = no_ratio,
    aes(x = 2020.5, y = 0.5),
    label = "No defined ratio",
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Region, ncol = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 17),
    labels = c("Other years", "2025 reporting caution")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2016, 2019, 2022, 2025)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.07))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Male-to-female rate ratio",
    shape = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```

### Interpretation, limitations, and stewardship

The analysis is descriptive and non-causal. We use PHAC's published crude
rates without age standardization, imputation, or hypothesis testing.
Age structure, small populations, varying reporting coverage, preliminary
investigations, and definition changes affect comparability.

Reported sex categories should not be equated with gender identity.
We preserve suppression and do not reconstruct suppressed counts or
identify people. These results can support further descriptive
investigation, but do not identify causes or establish which policy
response would be effective.

Source: [PHAC surveillance release](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/substance-related-harms/opioids-stimulants/).

Coverage and reporting cautions: [PHAC technical notes](https://health-infobase.canada.ca/substance-related-harms/opioids-stimulants/technical-notes.html).

## What the current evidence means for the audience

The stable finding for this draft is that PHAC's published Canada crude rate was higher in 2024 than in 2016 (16.2 versus 7.8 deaths per 100,000). The jurisdiction panels show substantial variation in reported rates and missingness. For a briefing, the figures help identify which regional patterns deserve closer source review and survey or demographic context. They do not justify a ranking of services or a causal explanation.

The decision needing feedback is whether thirteen small panels plus a Canada reference are readable for this audience, and whether the reporting cautions are prominent enough beside the 2025 observations. The male-to-female figure is secondary because several territorial or provincial ratios are undefined in the public release.

## Limitations and next step

The rates are crude, and comparisons may reflect age structure, population size, case definitions, investigation delays and reporting coverage. Recent observations can be revised. Suppressed or unavailable entries are kept missing, and the male-to-female ratio uses rounded source rates where both values are available and the female denominator is positive. The source's reported sex categories are not measures of gender identity. We will seek peer feedback on visual clarity, comparability and the placement of these cautions before finalizing the KT product.

## Reproducibility and AI audit

Render from the repository root with `quarto render milestones/m3-project-update/submission/report-draft.qmd`. The source reads the fixed CSV at `data/SubstanceHarmsData.csv` and generates the displayed tables, figures, and two CSV outputs. The methods and AI audit for the underlying analysis are in the M2 submission; the M3 AI-use note records the drafting work completed during M3.
